scope: Focused Snapshot hemodynamic physiology; no diagnostic criteria, drug doses or treatment targets

sources.title: Physiology, Cardiac Index
facts: Cardiac index expresses cardiac output relative to body surface area. An adult resting reference range is 2.5–4 L/min/m²; a value outside it requires clinical and measurement context rather than establishing a diagnosis.

sources.title: Shock — physiologic mechanisms
facts: Reduced filling can reduce stroke volume and cardiac output. Pump performance, rate/rhythm and mechanical restrictions can also affect flow. Vascular tone affects pressure and blood-flow distribution. These mechanisms may coexist; a monitor value does not establish their cause.

sources.title: Monitoring and Testing the Critical Care Patient
facts: Filling pressures are surrogates, not direct circulating-volume measurements. Flow, hemoglobin, oxygenation and demand together affect oxygen delivery. Perfusion observations, timed output and lactate need clinical context; ultrasound can assess ventricular function and mechanical restrictions.
